info.name: Direct SPI (without PO) — Stage 01 to Put-away
info.description:
SUPPLIER PURCHASE INVOICE RAISED WITHOUT A PURCHASE ORDER.

A Direct SPI is identified by `purchase_order_id IS NULL`. There is NO type flag and none should be added — everything conditional in this module keys off that null, and a second column saying the same thing is a second thing to keep in step.

What the purchase order used to supply now lives on the invoice itself: the shipment, the procurement case, TDS and the payment ledger.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BEFORE YOU START
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Migrations — both already applied on the dev database:
     2026_10_29_000001_direct_spi_links_tds_and_gst_approval
     2026_10_29_000002_allow_payments_against_a_direct_spi
   Verify:  php artisan migrate:status | grep 2026_10_29

2. Run folder 00 first. Login stores `token` and `branchId`.

3. Folders are numbered in execution order. 01 captures `spiId`,
   04 captures `spiItemId`, 05 captures `boxId`. Later calls read
   them from collection variables — do not skip ahead.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SEEDED TEST DATA (client 1)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  vendorId 3    S-003 — GST gate = approval_required. The ONLY state a
                senior can approve. Vendors 4 and 6 are `clear`;
                1, 2, 5, 7, 9, 10 are `blocked`. Both are refused.
  shipment 11   DSHP-001, carries proforma_invoice_id 4
  warehouse 1   WH-001, branch 3

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
KNOWN GAPS — read before reporting a bug
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A. document_type is REQUIRED by the API but is NOT collected by the
   Direct SPI setup modal (which asks only shipment, procurement,
   supplier). Every request here sends it explicitly. Not cosmetic:
   `international` short-circuits the GST gate to `clear`, and it is
   one of the two fields frozen once a senior approval exists.

B. A Direct SPI does NOT consume PI quantity. p2p_supplier_invoice_items
   has pi_item_id, but Stage 2 derives it from the PO line
   (`$po->pi_item_id`) and a direct line has no PO line — so it saves
   as null. pending_qty on the PI never decreases, and two Direct SPIs
   can each claim the same units. See folder 04.

C. PAYMENTS ARE BLOCKED for a Direct SPI. The endpoints exist but
   refuse it outright: "is a standalone invoice — it has no purchase
   order to pay against." The tables are open (purchase_order_id is
   nullable on both, supplier_invoice_id added to p2p_po_payments) but
   PoPaymentRequestController still takes a PurchaseOrder throughout.
   See folder 08.

D. ZOHO SYNC returns 501 for a standalone invoice — a pre-existing
   stub, not a regression. The schema is ready; only the sync is
   missing.

E. procurement_request_id is accepted but NOT validated against the
   `procurements` table, by request, while Step 02 is unwired. Restore
   the tenant fence when real ids start arriving.

variable.description: DSHP-001 — tenant-fenced; a foreign id returns 422
Active user of this client, in the invoice's branch, not you, not a client_admin

request.description:
Returns id, code, customer, consignee, opportunity_code, proforma_invoice_id, pi_number.

Shared with the PO create modal — these are master lookups, not PO data. Do NOT build an SPI twin: the same supplier would then read differently on two screens.

item.name: Supplier detail — ALSO answers the GST gate

request.description:
Call this on mount AND on every supplier change.

THERE IS NO GST-GATE ENDPOINT, by design. The browser computes the gate from the scrutiny and filing dates in THIS response, against a 3-month cutoff, exactly as PurchaseOrderService::gstGate() does server-side:

  no scrutiny, or scrutiny older than 3 months  -> blocked
  scrutiny current but filing older than 3 mo   -> approval_required
  both current                                  -> clear
  document_type = international                 -> clear (short-circuit)

Compare CALENDAR DATES, not rounded months. 2.96 months rounds to 3.0 and would block a supplier a day early.

The Evidence Vault (document completeness) is a SEPARATE, slower call. Fire it but do not await it — only the compliance card needs it, and awaiting both leaves the form on "Loading…".

query.description: with_po | without_po. Omit for the All SPI's tab.
with_shipment | without_shipment. Sub-filter on top of po_mode.

request.description:
THE LIST SCREEN — every tab and filter is this one endpoint.

TABS (po_mode + shipment_mode)
  All SPI's .................. omit po_mode entirely
  With Purchase Order SPI .... po_mode=with_po
  Without PO (Direct SPI) .... po_mode=without_po
    With Shipment ID ......... + shipment_mode=with_shipment
    All Other Transactions ... + shipment_mode=without_shipment

shipment_mode is a SUB-filter, not a replacement — it applies on top of
po_mode, and works under with_po too, since a PO-backed SPI can also be
with or without a shipment.

ALL ACCEPTED PARAMETERS (there are no others)
  po_mode        with_po | without_po
  shipment_mode  with_shipment | without_shipment
  status         draft | mapped | grn_pending | closed | cancelled
  vendor_id      integer
  from, to       dates (YYYY-MM-DD)
  q              free text, max 120 — SPI number, supplier, PO or status
  page           integer, min 1
  per_page       integer

MIND THE UNDERSCORES. `withpo` returns 422, not a full list. A mistyped
filter used to be ignored in silence and return every row, which reads as a
broken tab rather than a typo in the URL.

EVERY RESPONSE CARRIES THE SAME `counts` BLOCK — with_po, without_po,
with_shipment, without_shipment — so one request feeds all the tab badges.
The sub-tab counts add up to their parent.

KNOWN GAP — the Direct SPI sub-tabs are WRONG today:
  applyShipmentMode() asks the PURCHASE ORDER for the shipment
    whereHas('purchaseOrder', fn ($p) => $p->whereNotNull('shipment_order_id'))
  A Direct SPI has no PO, so that is always false. No Direct SPI can appear
  under With Shipment ID — even one created with shipment_order_id set — and
  all of them collapse into All Other Transactions.

  Two row columns are blank for the same reason:
    shipment_id     resolved from $po->shipment_order_id
    procurement_id  read from $po->procurement_request_code

  opportunity_id staying blank on a Direct SPI is CORRECT — it comes from
  the proforma invoice, which comes from the order.

  Needs the same `?? ` fallback already applied to the summary and the
  carton sticker: the invoice's own column first, then the order.

THIS IS THE "CREATE DRAFT" CALL. There is no separate mark-as-draft endpoint: the row is born with status=draft and stage_completed=1, and the code is allocated here.

The modal's Confirm & Continue should call exactly this after Steps 01–03.

`purchase_order_id: null` is what makes it direct.

All three links are OPTIONAL at the API — "All Other's (Without Shipment ID)" is a real answer to Step 01, not a skipped question.

shipment_order_id is TENANT-FENCED: an id belonging to another client returns 422, not a silent accept.
No shipment means NO PROFORMA INVOICE, so there is no PI quantity to check in Stage 02 — that stage becomes free entry. Run this variant separately; it does not overwrite {{spiId}}.

Same validator as create. Editable only while the invoice is a draft.

TWO GUARDS LIVE HERE:
  · the purchase order cannot be re-pointed once items exist
  · the supplier and document_type freeze once a GST approval exists (folder 02)
MUST return 422. An unscoped ['nullable','integer'] would accept this, including another client's row — the exact bug the warehouse_id rule in this validator documents.

item.name: 02 · GST senior approval
C0 · Who can approve (pick the senior)

request.description: Active users of this client, minus the caller, with department and designation. The id you pick goes in requested_to below. A Direct SPI approval stops at the branch head, so the senior must sit in the invoice's branch.

exec: // Anyone but the caller, active, in this branch. Take the first.

item.name: C · Raise the approval against the SPI

request.description:
Only a DIRECT SPI may raise its own: a PO-backed invoice is refused (422) and sends its order instead — one supplier risk, one approval.

requested_to is required, EXCEPT when the last approval on this invoice was rejected: it then goes back to the same senior and any requested_to sent is ignored.

Refused (422) when: the invoice is cancelled · no supplier on Stage 01 · GST scrutiny itself is older than 3 months (nobody can approve past that — update the scrutiny) · the gate is already clear (nothing to approve) · one is already pending · already approved · the approver is not an active user of this client, is outside the invoice's branch, or is you.

exec: pm.test('hangs off the invoice, not an order', () => {

item.name: R · This invoice's approvals (history + live gate)

request.description:
The requester's view: every approval ever raised against THIS invoice, newest first, plus the GST gate read live.

Tenant-fenced on client_id, so another client's invoice id gives 404. Not branch-fenced — the approver may sit in another branch and the requester still needs the history.

Alongside the rows, `gst` carries { gate, gstin, scrutiny_date, filing_date, stale_months }. gate is why the approval exists at all: approval_required means the return is overdue, blocked means the scrutiny itself is stale and no senior can approve past it.

exec: // gate: blocked | approval_required | clear — read live, not at request time.

request.description:
Run this AS THE APPROVER (log in as the user in approverUserId). It lists only requests sent to the caller.

Query: history=0 (default) → still pending, oldest request first; history=1 → decided only, newest decision first. per_page 1–50, default 10.

One row shape for either subject: po_code carries the INVOICE code when subject_type is supplier_invoice, and po_date carries invoice_date. supplier_invoice_id tells you which it was. gst_last_filing_date is null for a Direct SPI — that column lives on the PO.

pm.test('the SPI-raised request is visible', () => pm.expect(mine).to.not.eql(undefined));

request.description:
Readable by the approver OR the requester; anyone else gets 403.

The `po` block is the subject's header whichever it is — for a Direct SPI it carries the invoice code, invoice_date as po_date, its totals and its own shipment_code / procurement_code. The order-only terms (po_type, mode_of_transport, Incoterm, ports, shipping / packaging / other charges, physical_inspection) come back null, so the screen keeps one shape and prints a dash. tax_mode is derived from total_igst, not stored.

`lines` are the invoice's items, each with its own description / HSN / UOM. `gst` is the gate read live, so the senior sees today's position, not the one at request time. `can_decide` is true only for the chosen senior, while pending, and while the invoice is neither cancelled nor deleted.

exec: // From the SPI's own columns, not through a PO.

item.name: U · Decide — approve or reject (as the approver)

request.description:
The field is `decision`, not status: approved | rejected. `reason` is required either way, max 1000 chars.

Only the senior it was sent to may decide (403 otherwise), only while pending (422 if already decided), and not if the invoice has been cancelled or deleted.

A PO caches the verdict in its own gst_approval_* columns. A Direct SPI has none by design — this approval row IS the record, read back through the invoice's approvals. So after this call, re-read 'R · This invoice's approvals' rather than looking for a field on the invoice.

Rejected does not free the invoice: raising again goes back to the SAME senior, and any requested_to you send is ignored.

item.name: 422 · a PO-backed invoice cannot raise its own

request.description: Set spiWithPoId to any SPI that HAS a purchase_order_id. Its supplier risk is the order's, and the order's approval already covers this invoice; allowing both would leave two approvals free to disagree.

item.name: 422 · supplier locked once sent to a senior

request.description:
Once an approval is pending OR approved, the supplier and document_type are frozen: the senior judged THAT supplier's GST. Changing either would leave an approval describing a risk the invoice no longer carries.

All the other Stage 01 fields stay editable. To change the supplier, the approval has to be rejected first.

item.description:
GST senior approval, raised against the SPI id.

It exists because the supplier's last GST return is overdue: the gate reads the latest vendor_gst_scrutiny row against a 3-month cutoff and answers blocked / approval_required / clear. Only approval_required can be sent to a senior. An international invoice short-circuits to clear and needs no approval at all.

Create and the per-invoice history are keyed on {{spiId}}. Reading one and deciding it are keyed on the APPROVAL id, under /p2p/orders/ — one approver screen serves both documents, so there is no /p2p/spi mirror for them.

Order to run: C0 → C → R (history) → log in as the approver → R (inbox) → R (one) → U.

request.description:
WHERE STAGE 02's ITEM DETAIL COMES FROM.

Per line: pi_item_id, product_id, product_code, product_name, hsn_code, uom, rate, gst_pct, description, pi_quantity, ordered_qty, PENDING_QTY.
Plus `held_by` — which POs hold the rest, so an empty Stage 02 explains itself instead of showing a bare zero.

A shipment with no PI returns proforma_invoice_id: null and lines: [] — it does not error.

HELD = a PO that is submitted OR has a pending/approved GST approval, AND is not cancelled. That last clause was added with this work: a cancelled PO with an approved request held PI quantity for ever, so no later PO or Direct SPI could claim it.

CAVEAT: `exclude_po` takes a PO id only. A Direct SPI has none, so on EDIT it cannot exclude its own lines and pending_qty reads low. Needs an exclude_spi equivalent.

request.description:
THE WHOLE GRID SAVES AT ONCE — never row by row. The header totals are rolled up from the lines in the same transaction, so a partial save would leave the two disagreeing.

THE TOTALS YOU SEND ARE OVERWRITTEN. rollupTotals() recomputes taxable_total, total_cgst/sgst/igst and grand_total by SUMming the saved lines. If your arithmetic is off, the LINES win — read the response, not your payload.

THE SERVER DOES NOT SPLIT GST. cgst/sgst vs igst is decided by the caller from the supplier's state code. Interstate: igst_amount = 132, cgst = sgst = 0.

`po_item_id: null` — a direct line stands on its own, and that field was ALREADY nullable, so Stage 02 needed no change for this feature.

What does NOT apply to a direct line: qty_open / qty_over / closed all come from the PO balance. There is no order to exceed, so over-supply detection is simply absent.

>>> GAP B: pi_item_id saves as NULL. writeItems() derives it from the PO
>>> line (`$po->pi_item_id`) and a direct line has none. Re-run folder 03
>>> after this and pending_qty is UNCHANGED — the units are on the invoice
>>> but invisible to the PI ledger, so two Direct SPIs can claim the same
>>> quantity. Fix needs: accept items.*.pi_item_id, store it, and teach
>>> orderedByPiItem() to count Direct SPI lines.

Same endpoint, multipart. POST rather than PUT because PHP does not populate $_FILES on a PUT.

DO NOT set Content-Type by hand — the client adds multipart/form-data with the boundary. Setting it manually drops the boundary and Laravel sees an empty body.

OMIT po_item_id entirely. In form-data every value is text, so "null" arrives as a 4-character string and fails the integer rule.

Both files are optional: pdf/jpg/jpeg/png/webp, max 10 MB.
Moves the invoice off draft. Stage 01 is no longer editable afterwards — isEditable() keys off the draft status.

PO-INDEPENDENT ALREADY. Reads SupplierInvoiceItem and p2p_spi_box_items; never the order. qty_pending = qty_spi - qty_packed.

Nothing in Stage 03 or Stage 04 was changed for Direct SPI — they were already keyed to the invoice.
Preview only — the code that lands in the database is allocated on save.

SCENARIOS
  s1  1 product  -> 1 box        (refused with more than 1 product)
  s2  1 product  -> many boxes   (refused with more than 1 product)
  s3  many products -> 1 box     (refused with fewer than 2 products)

CONDITION: perfect | minor | major | severe.

CHECK ON A DIRECT SPI: the PROCUREMENT box must print the invoice's own code, not a dash. It reads `spi.procurement_request_code ?? po?.procurement_request_code` — before this work a direct SPI printed a dash for a carton that IS against a case.

PURCHASE ORDER correctly stays a dash — there is no order.

The QR carries a SIGNED URL (HMAC), not the box code. The put-away scanner matches on that URL — do not swap it for bare text.

Stamps sticker_printed_at on first download: a label in hand is a label about to go on a carton.
The Temporary Storage Selection modal: storage type -> warehouse -> confirm. `own` enables the full put-away flow with rack/shelf allocation; a third-party warehouse is summary-only.
Driven from the BOXES, so a box nobody has started still appears. ZERO PO references anywhere in the four SpiPutaway* controllers.

Without `mode` only the two counts the opening modal needs; with it the whole tree AND the recommendation.

If eligible comes back 0, the response carries a `diagnosis` block saying WHY — requirement met nowhere, met separately but never together, or handling fine and it is space or a lock.

POST, not PUT: each scan stamps its own timestamp, so it is not idempotent.

Send the FULL SIGNED URL from the sticker, not the box code — the scanner matches on that payload.

THREE THINGS TO CHECK on a Direct SPI:

  spi_type       'Direct SPI'  — derived from the null order, not a flag
  shipment_id    the Step 01 shipment, NOT null
  procurement_id the Step 02 code, NOT null

Both used to resolve ONLY through the purchase order, so a Direct SPI reported neither even when both had been chosen. They now read the invoice first and fall back to the order.

  opportunity_id stays null, correctly — it comes from the PI, which comes from the order.
The SUPPLIER's vault is a different endpoint: /segment-uploads/supplier/{id}/vault.

exec: pm.test('ledger falls back to the invoice', () => pm.expect(d.ledger.source).to.eql('supplier_invoice'));

request.description:
THE READ SIDE WORKS. p2p_po_payment_requests already carries supplier_invoice_id, so the per-invoice history is genuinely keyed to the invoice.

`ledger` is new and is what the screen should read. The ceiling used to be returned only as `po`, which is null on a Direct SPI, leaving nothing to validate against. `ledger` NAMES its source:

  source = purchase_order     PO-backed: the order's balance, unchanged
  source = supplier_invoice   Direct: the invoice's own tds/paid/balance

net_payable = grand_total - tds_amount on both sides. TDS is cut on the TAXABLE base, not the grand total — GST is not subject to TDS.

paid_amount is NULL until the first payment. "The ledger has not been opened" is not the same as a zero balance, which is why the column has no 0.00 default.

EXPECTED 422: "... is a standalone invoice — it has no purchase order to pay against."

storeFromSpi() reads the invoice's purchase_order_id and hands over to the PO flow. With no order there is nothing to hand to.

The SCHEMA is ready (purchase_order_id nullable on both payment tables, supplier_invoice_id on p2p_po_payments). What is missing is the controller: payable() gates on PO state (isCancelled / status=submitted / signingStarted), saveTds() computes on $order->taxable_total and writes to the order, and the SPI is validated as BELONGING to a PO.

It needs the same subject-based refactor already applied to PoGstApprovalController.

EXPECTED 501: "Zoho sync for standalone invoices is not wired up yet."

PRE-EXISTING STUB, not a regression. The schema is ready — zoho_bill_id, zoho_bill_number, zoho_status, zoho_error and zoho_synced_at are already on the invoice, and ownsZohoBill() already returns isStandalone(), so a Direct SPI is ALREADY the owner of its own bill by design. Only the sync code is missing.

A PO-backed invoice is refused differently: its bill belongs to the order.
Says WHY there is no bill, rather than showing an empty state.
